adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:333 — Org/team scope tests only compare Prisma.sql text with toEqual and never execute it, so runtime failures in the `= ANY(${array})` typing, column names or precedence would still pass (only user scope runs, line 481).

adjudication.rationale: In the updated integration tests, most org/team scope cases assert `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` (e.g., the org/team authorization condition expectations using `= ANY(${[...]})`), but they never actually run those `Prisma.Sql` fragments against the database. The only place the SQL is executed in this diff is the new `getBaseConditions` test which uses `prisma.$queryRaw` with `WHERE ${baseConditions}`, and that test is configured with `scope: "user"` (not org/team). So errors in the org/team SQL (column names, operator precedence, or array typing for `ANY`) could slip through while tests still pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:75 — getBaseConditions returns the org/team `(A) OR (B)` fragment without outer parentheses when there are no filters, so a caller's `WHERE ${base} AND <predicate>` drops that predicate for the A branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `getBaseConditions()`, when there are no filters it returns `authConditions` directly (no wrapping): `else if (authConditions) { return authConditions; }`. For org/team scopes, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` construct an OR expression via `reduce` as `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})``, yielding a top-level SQL fragment like `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses. If a caller later composes `WHERE ${base} AND <predicate>`, SQL precedence makes it parse as `A OR (B AND <predicate>)`, so `<predicate>` does not apply to the A branch. This is a correctness defect in the new SQL-fragment API introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:106 — Public getFilterConditions returns a bare `eventTypeId = x OR eventParentId = x`, so composing `${auth} AND ${filter}` matches bookings outside the authorized scope.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `getBaseConditions()` composes conditions as `Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})`` (with parentheses around both sides). Even though `buildFilterConditions()` may return a single SQL fragment like `("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)`, it is still wrapped in parentheses when combined with auth, so it will not escape the authorized scope due to SQL operator precedence. The tests were updated accordingly to expect `((eventTypeId=...) OR (eventParentId=...)) AND (userId=...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 — Loose InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions lets `scope: "team"` without teamId type-check, and zod then silently nulls the options so insights come back empty instead of failing at compile time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `teamId?: number` and changes the constructor to accept that looser type (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`) while internal logic relies on zod’s discriminated union (`insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema`) where `scope: "team"` requires `teamId`. This is a type-safety regression: callers can now compile with `{scope:"team", userId, orgId}` lacking `teamId`, and the service can end up with `this.options` invalid/null (the class explicitly allows `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null` and `buildAuthorizationConditions()` returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` when `!this.options`). The claim that zod “silently nulls” can’t be fully verified from the shown diff because the constructor’s parse/safeParse assignment isn’t visible here, but the loosened typing issue is directly grounded.

In `insightsBooking.ts`, caching still exists via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` (now `Prisma.Sql`), but no replacement tests were added to verify this caching behavior after the refactor to SQL conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 — New InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (flat, teamId optional) replaces the discriminated-union type in the constructor at :58, so `{scope:"team"}` without teamId type-checks but fails safeParse, and the service silently returns `1=0` (empty results) rather than a compile error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `scope: "user" | "org" | "team"` and `teamId?: number`, and changes the constructor to accept this flat type (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`). That removes compile-time enforcement that `teamId` is required when `scope === "team"`. The service still internally expects `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the zod discriminated union) and uses `NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0`` as the fail-closed path when `this.options` is null/invalid (`buildAuthorizationConditions(): if (!this.options) return NOTHING_CONDITION;`). So an invalid `{ scope: "team", ... }` without `teamId` can now type-check and will be treated as “no access” at runtime (empty results) rather than being rejected by TypeScript. This is a type-safety/API contract regression created by the change, even though it fails closed.

OR (eventParentId=..)` at :106, org/team `(A) OR (B)` at :173/:206), so any consumer that composes them as `WHERE x AND ${cond}` gets the wrong operator precedence; the old WhereInput objects were self-contained.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `getFilterConditions()` / `getAuthorizationConditions()` now return `Prisma.Sql` fragments that can contain top-level `OR` without being wrapped as a whole expression (e.g. `buildFilterConditions()` returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)`, and org/team builders reduce with `(${acc}) OR (${condition})` but do not wrap the final result). If a caller interpolates these into a larger `WHERE x AND ${cond}`, SQL operator precedence could change semantics unless the caller adds parentheses. However, within this diff the only demonstrated composition is `getBaseConditions()`, which *does* wrap both sides when combining (`Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})\``), so an actual broken behavior for existing consumers is not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 — Public findMany (typed Prisma rows, select/where merge) was removed and replaced by getBaseConditions returning raw Prisma.Sql, which pushes untyped $queryRaw and unqualified column names (no table alias, ambiguous under joins) onto every caller, with no deprecation path; this snapshot contains no other callers to confirm the impact.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` being removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` (insightsBooking.ts). All condition builders now return raw SQL fragments via `Prisma.sql` (e.g., `("userId" = ...) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)`), which cannot be passed into Prisma `findMany` `where` clauses as before, so callers are effectively forced toward raw querying. The integration test demonstrates this new usage by switching to `$queryRaw` with `WHERE ${baseConditions}`. The concern about unqualified column names is grounded (the SQL uses bare quoted columns without table alias), though whether that becomes ambiguous depends on unseen caller queries/joins, so the impact on “every caller” can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:83 — getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions and the public build* methods (:97, :125) changed their return type from Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput to Prisma.Sql, which breaks the contract for any consumer that spreads them into a Prisma `where`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the return types of getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions (and build* helpers) from Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput to Prisma.Sql (see cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions and method signatures). That means any external consumer that previously did something like `where: { AND: [await svc.getAuthorizationConditions(), ...] }` would no longer be able to, since Prisma.Sql isn’t a valid `where` input. The diff itself doesn’t show such consumers, so the impact can’t be fully verified here, but the contract/type change is real and potentially breaking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:74 — When no filters are set, getBaseConditions returns the org/team auth fragment `(A) OR (B)` without outer parentheses, so a caller writing `WHERE ${base} AND <extra>` gets `A OR (B AND extra)` and leaks rows past the extra predicate (the old findMany kept auth isolated inside its own AND array)

adjudication.rationale: In getBaseConditions(), when filterConditions is null it returns authConditions directly (no wrapping): `else if (authConditions) { return authConditions; }`. For org/team scopes, buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition build an OR expression like `(...team...) OR (...user...)` via `reduce` (it parenthesizes operands but not the whole expression). If a caller later embeds this fragment into a larger WHERE like `WHERE ${base} AND extra`, SQL operator precedence makes it `A OR (B AND extra)` instead of `(A OR B) AND extra`, which can broaden results compared to the previous `findMany` AND-array isolation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:106 — A single eventTypeId filter comes back from getFilterConditions as a bare `(x) OR (y)` with no outer parentheses, so any caller that combines it with AND directly has the same precedence bug

adjudication.rationale: In `buildFilterConditions`, the `eventTypeId` clause is returned as a raw `Prisma.sql` fragment `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` with no outer parentheses. Within this PR’s own usage (`getBaseConditions`) it is safely wrapped as `(${filterConditions})` before being `AND`’d, so the precedence bug described does not occur in the shown code path. However, since `getFilterConditions()` is public and returns that bare OR fragment, it is a real API footgun: any external caller that interpolates it into a larger SQL expression without adding parentheses could get incorrect precedence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:58 — The constructor now takes the loose InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (teamId optional, scope is a plain union), so `{scope:"team"}` without teamId now compiles, fails zod safeParse, and quietly returns 1=0 (no data) instead of being caught at compile time

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the constructor parameter type from the zod-derived `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to a looser `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `scope` is a plain union and `teamId` is optional. Meanwhile `buildAuthorizationConditions()` returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` (`Prisma.sql`1=0``) when `this.options` is null, and `this.options` is still intended to be validated against `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` (hence invalid options can become null). Therefore `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` can now compile but be rejected at runtime and yield `1=0`, which is a real, diff-grounded API/type-safety regression. It’s not a guaranteed runtime defect unless a caller omits `teamId`, but it makes misconfiguration easier and failures silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:76 — authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object, so the filter-only and NOTHING_CONDITION branches can never run; the filter-only branch is also misleading because it would return filters with no authorization if it ever did run

adjudication.rationale: In `getBaseConditions()`, `authConditions` is typed/implemented as `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and `buildAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` (including `NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0`` when unauthorized / missing options). A `Prisma.Sql` object is always truthy, so `else if (filterConditions)` and the final `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branches are dead code as written; the function will always return either `(${auth}) AND (${filter})` (when filters exist) or just `authConditions` (when `filterConditions` is `null`). This is a real, diff-grounded issue (unreachable/misleading branching), but it doesn’t by itself demonstrate broken behavior from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:10 — Test re-declares NOTHING_CONDITION as a copy of the private module constant instead of importing a shared export, so the sentinel can drift between service and tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a module-level `NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0`` constant added in the service (`insightsBooking.ts`) but it is not exported, and the integration test file separately declares its own `const NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0`` (line added near the top). This duplicates the sentinel condition across files; if the service’s sentinel changes later, tests could silently diverge unless they share an exported constant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:437 — The Caching describe block was deleted even though the caching fields/getters still exist unchanged, leaving the cache behavior untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching")` block in `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` (removed tests that called `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` twice). However, the service still implements caching via `private cachedAuthConditions?: Prisma.Sql; private cachedFilterConditions?: Prisma.Sql | null;` and the getters memoize results when the cache is `undefined` (`getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions`). This leaves the caching behavior untested after the refactor to `Prisma.Sql` conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:159 — Org scope loads every membership row for the org and all its sub-teams into memory (no DISTINCT, deduped in JS), then sends the whole user ID list back as a single ANY() array param; this grows with org size and could be replaced by an in-SQL subquery now that the conditions are raw SQL

adjudication.rationale: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the org scope still fetches all memberships for all org teams via `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds(...)`, maps them to `userIdsFromOrg`, then dedupes in JS (`Array.from(new Set(userIdsFromOrg))`) and embeds the full list into a raw SQL condition using `"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`. This matches the finding: it scales with org size, loads rows into memory, and sends a potentially large array parameter. The diff’s shift to raw SQL (`Prisma.Sql`) makes an in-SQL subquery a plausible improvement, but this is a performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:164 — The generated auth predicate `(teamId = ANY(..) AND isTeamBooking) OR (userId = ANY(..) AND NOT isTeamBooking)` is a top-level OR across two different columns, which Postgres can only serve with a BitmapOr or a seq scan; this is still true after the raw-SQL rewrite, which missed the chance to use a UNION or a subquery

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly constructs a top-level SQL OR predicate combining different columns: in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` it returns `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}) AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR ("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds}) AND "isTeamBooking" = false)` via `conditions.reduce(... OR ...)` (around the cited area). That matches the finding’s predicate shape and remains after the raw-SQL rewrite. This is a performance/query-planning concern (may force BitmapOr/seq scan) rather than a correctness defect, and the suggested alternative (UNION/subquery) is an optimization opportunity, not a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:106 — Public getFilterConditions()/getAuthorizationConditions() return unparenthesized OR fragments (eventType filter line 106, org/team auth reduce at 171-174/204-207), so any caller interpolating them as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${x}` instead of via getBaseConditions lets the OR branch bypass the auth predicate and leak cross-org bookings

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions() to return raw Prisma.Sql fragments. Several of those fragments contain top-level ORs without wrapping parentheses around the whole expression (e.g. buildFilterConditions eventTypeId returns `("eventTypeId"=...) OR ("eventParentId"=...)`, and org/team auth conditions are built via an OR-reduce that yields `(... ) OR (...)` without an outer `(...)`). Within this PR, getBaseConditions correctly guards precedence by emitting `(${auth}) AND (${filter})`, so there’s no demonstrated leak in the shown usage/tests. However, because these methods remain public, they are easy to misuse by callers composing `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}` without extra parentheses, which would change semantics due to SQL AND/OR precedence. The finding’s concrete “leak” depends on external callers not shown in the diff, so it’s a real API/footgun concern but not a verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:76 — getBaseConditions has a fail-open branch returning filter-only conditions (no auth) when auth is falsy; currently unreachable since auth is always a Prisma.Sql, but it replaces the old always-AND-with-NOTHING semantics and would silently drop authorization if auth ever became null

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getBaseConditions()` implementation, there is an explicit branch `else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }` which would drop authorization entirely if `authConditions` were ever falsy. In this diff, `getAuthorizationConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` always returns a `Prisma.sql` object (including `NOTHING_CONDITION`), so the fail-open path is currently unreachable. However, the code structure does encode a potentially risky future behavior change compared to the old `findMany` logic which always ANDed auth with filters (auth was never nullable), so a later refactor that makes auth nullable could silently become filter-only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:295 — Team and org scope auth tests only compare Prisma.sql objects via toEqual and never run the new raw SQL (ANY(array) params, quoted columns, OR/AND nesting), so a wrong column name, bad array binding, or cross-team/org leak would still pass

adjudication.rationale: In the updated integration tests, the org/team authorization cases now assert `await service.getAuthorizationConditions()` with `expect(...).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` (e.g., around the former lines ~296 and ~346), but they do not execute those conditions against the database. Since `Prisma.Sql` is just a structured object, these assertions won’t catch issues like misquoted/incorrect column names, incorrect `ANY(${array})` binding, or OR/AND grouping that only manifests when used in a real `WHERE` clause. Only the later `getBaseConditions` test actually runs `$queryRaw ... WHERE ${baseConditions}`, and it covers the combined/base path, not specifically validating org/team auth conditions in execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:437 — Converting findMany to getBaseConditions left one executed-query test (user scope only), so no test runs org/team scope SQL against the DB to show bookings from other orgs/teams are excluded

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous `findMany` execution-based coverage and replaces it with a single executed-query test under `describe("getBaseConditions")` that runs `prisma.$queryRaw` with `baseConditions` (and it uses `scope: "user"`). The other scope cases (org/team) are only asserted via `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` and never used in an actual DB query to validate that the generated SQL correctly excludes bookings from other orgs/teams. So the finding about missing executed-query coverage for org/team scopes is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:480 — The only DB-executing test can't catch AND/OR precedence mistakes in getBaseConditions because no seeded booking matches the filter but fails auth (e.g. another user's booking on the same eventType or a child with eventParentId)

adjudication.rationale: In the updated integration test, the only DB-executing assertion for `getBaseConditions()` runs a raw query and expects exactly one row (the `userBooking`). However, the diff does not show any additional seeded bookings that would also satisfy the filter portion (e.g., same `eventTypeId`/`eventParentId`) while failing the authorization portion. Without such negative fixtures, the test could still pass even if `getBaseConditions()` had an AND/OR grouping/precedence bug that unintentionally broadened results, because there’s no competing row to be accidentally included. This is a specific coverage gap introduced/left by the change from Prisma where-inputs to SQL fragments and raw SQL evaluation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 — getBaseConditions branches are untested: auth-only with no filters, NOTHING_CONDITION auth plus filters (non-admin with filters must return zero rows), and the unreachable filter-only/NOTHING fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial branching in `getBaseConditions()` (auth+filter, auth-only, filter-only, and both-null fallback to `NOTHING_CONDITION`) in `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` lines ~65-84. The updated integration test suite adds coverage for the auth+filter combination via `describe("getBaseConditions")`, but there is no test shown for (a) auth-only when `filters` are not provided (so `getFilterConditions()` returns `null`), (b) non-admin/auth returning `NOTHING_CONDITION` combined with non-null filters to ensure the final condition still yields zero rows, or (c) the both-null fallback path. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:207 — Team and org builders now drop the userId branch when the member list is empty (was userId IN []), and org with no child teams binds ANY([orgId]), but no test covers the empty teamIds/userIds cases

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites authorization builders to return raw SQL using `ANY(${array})` (e.g., `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` and `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))`). The new code conditionally omits the userId branch when the user ID list is empty in the team/org builders, and the tests updated in this PR only cover non-empty arrays. While the finding’s claim that org previously produced `userId IN []` is not supported (old org code already skipped that branch when empty), it’s still a valid, diff-grounded review concern that there’s no test coverage for empty `teamIds`/`userIds` edge cases under the new raw-SQL/`ANY(...)` construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:384 — The eventTypeId filter's eventParentId branch is only checked as SQL text and never run, so no test confirms bookings of child (managed) event types are matched

adjudication.rationale: In the updated tests, the eventTypeId filter is validated only by asserting `getFilterConditions()` equals a `Prisma.sql` fragment like `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` (see the changed expectation around the filter conditions test). No test executes a query that would actually prove the `eventParentId` branch matches bookings for a child/managed event type. The only query-executing test in this diff (`getBaseConditions` + `$queryRaw`) asserts a single booking match and does not demonstrate a booking matched via `eventParentId` specifically. This is a concrete coverage gap introduced/exposed by switching expectations to SQL fragments, but not a demonstrated functional defect in the service code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:273 — Exact Prisma.sql toEqual expectations are tied to whitespace and parenthesization, so harmless SQL reformatting breaks tests while semantically wrong SQL still passes

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes multiple integration test assertions from structural Prisma `WhereInput` objects to exact `Prisma.sql` template literals, e.g. `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`("userId" = ${testData.user.id}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)`)` and similar OR/AND expressions. `toEqual` on a `Prisma.Sql` object will compare its underlying `strings` (and value placeholders), so harmless changes in whitespace/parenthesization in the SQL template will break these tests even if semantics are unchanged. This is a test brittleness/maintainability concern created by the change, not a runtime correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:437 — The Caching describe block was deleted even though cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions still exist, and the swap to Prisma.Sql caching is no longer tested

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the entire `describe("Caching")` block from `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts`, which previously verified that repeated calls to `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the cached result. In the service (`insightsBooking.ts`), caching still exists via `cachedAuthConditions?: Prisma.Sql` and `cachedFilterConditions?: Prisma.Sql | null`, with logic in `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()` that only builds once when the cached value is `undefined`. Since the caching mechanism changed type from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`, the deleted tests mean this nontrivial behavior is no longer covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:332 — The org scope expectation relies on the order of teamIds/userIds from unordered repository queries (findAllByParentId, findAllByTeamIds), so it can fail depending on DB row order

adjudication.rationale: The org-scope test now asserts equality against a specific `Prisma.sql` object containing `ANY(${[...]})` arrays in a fixed order (e.g. `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`). But `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition()` constructs `teamIds` and `userIdsFromOrg` via repository queries (`findAllByParentId`, `findAllByTeamIds`) and maps them without sorting, and also preserves insertion order when de-duping via `new Set(userIdsFromOrg)`. If those repos return rows in non-deterministic order, the produced `Prisma.Sql` will embed arrays in a different order, making `expect(conditions).toEqual(...)` flaky even though the SQL semantics are order-insensitive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 — The new looser InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type allows scope "team" without teamId, which silently falls back to NOTHING_CONDITION, and no test covers this

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `teamId?: number` and changes the constructor to accept this looser type (`constructor ... options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`). For `scope: "team"`, `buildAuthorizationConditions()` unconditionally calls `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition(this.options)`, which then uses `options.teamId` in `findByIdAndParentId({ id: options.teamId, parentId: options.orgId })`. If `teamId` is omitted/undefined, `childTeamOfOrg` will be falsy and the method returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` (`Prisma.sql\`1=0\``), silently producing no results instead of rejecting invalid options. The tests updated in this diff cover SQL condition construction, but none cover the `scope: "team"` without `teamId` case.
